modelType.help: The form of the response surface. Quadratic and "Linear + interaction" both compute z = β₀ + β₁·x + β₂·y + β₃·x² + β₄·y² + β₅·x·y with all six coefficients; the only difference is the name of the choice. With "Custom formula" the formula in x and y applies instead of the coefficients.

b.help: The six coefficients β₀…β₅ of the model, without effect with a custom formula; the fields run from β₀ to β₅. There are always exactly six numbers.

customFormula.help: The own formula for z in the variables x and y. Allowed are numbers, the operators + − * / ^ and **, parentheses, constants such as PI and E, and functions such as sin, cos, tan, exp, sqrt, abs, log (base 10), ln (natural), min, max and pow; a Math. prefix is optional, angles are in radians. An invalid formula is accepted and reported below the formula. It applies only with a custom formula.

xLabel.help: The name of the X factor; it appears as the axis title and in the hint at the pointer. Empty means "Factor X". An axis title from the chart editor takes precedence.

yLabel.help: The name of the Y factor; it appears as the axis title and in the hint at the pointer. Empty means "Factor Y". An axis title from the chart editor takes precedence.

zLabel.help: The name of the response (Z); it appears in the chart title and in the hint at the pointer. Empty means "Response Z".

xMin.help: The lower end of the X axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from X min to X max. X min must be smaller than X max, otherwise the value is rejected. To move the range upward, set X max first and then X min; to move it downward, the other way round.

xMax.help: The upper end of the X axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from X min to X max. X max must be greater than X min, otherwise the value is rejected. To move the range upward, set X max first and then X min; to move it downward, the other way round.

yMin.help: The lower end of the Y axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from Y min to Y max. Y min must be smaller than Y max, otherwise the value is rejected. To move the range upward, set Y max first and then Y min; to move it downward, the other way round.

yMax.help: The upper end of the Y axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from Y min to Y max. Y max must be greater than Y min, otherwise the value is rejected. To move the range upward, set Y max first and then Y min; to move it downward, the other way round.

datasets.help: The three columns of the measured points, each described individually under keys. With all three set, the chart shows the measured points over the surface.

x.label: X
x.title: The column of the X values (slot x), numeric, optional
x.help: The column of the X values (slot x), optional: measured points over the surface once all three slots are chosen. Empty while none is chosen.

y.label: Y
y.title: The column of the Y values (slot y), numeric, optional
y.help: The column of the Y values (slot y), optional: measured points over the surface once all three slots are chosen. Empty while none is chosen.

z.label: Z
z.title: The column of the measured response (slot z), numeric, optional
z.help: The column of the measured response (slot z), optional: measured points over the surface once all three slots are chosen. Empty while none is chosen.

exampleWorksheetId.help: The id of the worksheet a loaded example created; null without an example sheet. Not meant to be set by hand.

chartEdits.help: The settings from the chart editor: title, axis titles, font sizes, background, reference lines and areas, color scheme, contour levels, grid resolution, lines, labels, measured points and their markers. Only deviations from the defaults are stored.

formulaError.help: The rejection of the custom formula, each entry described individually under keys; null while the formula is valid or no custom formula is in use.

activeParams.help: The fields that apply to the chosen model form: with a custom formula customFormula instead of b.

surface.help: The figures of the evaluated surface over the axis range: smallest and largest value, range and optimum, each described individually under keys; null with an error in the custom formula.

dataPoints.help: The measured points from the three columns, paired row by row; rows without three numbers are left out. Empty while a column is missing.

surfaceGrid.help: The sampled surface the chart, the cards, the legend and the table export are built from: the grid with the smallest and largest value and the optimum. With an error in the custom formula the values count as 0 (a flat surface).

chart.help: The configuration of the contour chart: grid, axis ranges, measured points and the defaults for the title and axis titles, which the chart editor can override.

Surface.zMin: The smallest value of the surface. The surface is evaluated on a grid of 100 × 100 points (default; adjustable in the chart editor under "Grid resolution") over the axis range; the "Z Min" card shows the value.
Surface.zMax: The largest value of the surface on the same grid; the "Z Max" card shows the value.
Surface.range: The range of the surface, largest minus smallest value (Z max − Z min); the "Z Range" card shows it and below it the number of contour levels.
Surface.optimum: The highest point of the grid. The "Optimum (Max)" card shows its value and below it its x and y; with equally high points the first in grid order counts.

SurfacePoint.x: The X value of the point on the grid.
SurfacePoint.y: The Y value of the point on the grid.
SurfacePoint.z: The value of the surface at this point.

FormulaError.code: The kind of error: illegal character, invalid number, empty formula, syntax error, surplus characters at the end, unknown variable (only x and y are allowed) or unknown function. The interface shows the translated text for it below the formula.
FormulaError.token: The offending character, the invalid number, or the unknown variable or function; it appears in the text below the formula. With an empty formula, a syntax error and surplus characters it is missing.

DataPoint.x: The value of the x column in this row.
DataPoint.y: The value of the y column in this row.
DataPoint.z: The value of the z column in this row.
